summary: Order quote timeouts are caused by pricing-engine CPU saturation triggered by the feature-flag ramp cfg-3120 (flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5->100 at 12:04), which moved (almost) all quotes onto the expensive GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (20000 paths, 3-9s each). pricing-engine CPU went 40%->99%, p99 went 60ms->~2600ms against a 2000ms quote budget, and order-service quote calls began timing out at 2500ms from 12:06. The market-data-service protobuf deploy (dep-6111 at 11:56) named in the report is NOT the cause: its error_rate and latency are perfectly flat. Request rate is flat, ruling out a capacity/traffic surge. Fault originates in pricing-engine configuration => config_change; the fix is to roll back cfg-3120.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Feature-flag ramp of CPU-heavy Greeks v2 calculator saturated pricing-engine CPU
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-3120 ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100 at 12:04, switching virtually all quote computations to the expensive GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (20000 paths, 3-9s each). This pegged pricing-engine CPU at ~99%, pushed p99 above the 2000ms budget, and caused the downstream order-service quote-call timeouts. The fault originates in pricing-engine's configuration, not in market-data-service.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-3120 ramps greeks_v2 rollout from 5% to 100% at 12:04
GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator consumes 3-9s CPU per quote (20000 paths)
pricing-engine CPU saturates at ~99% with flat request rate
p99 exceeds the 2000ms quote budget -> deadline-exceeded errors
order-service quote calls exceed 2500ms and time out

assumptions: greeks_v2.rollout_pct=100 means all/almost all quote requests use the GreeksV2 calculator
CPU saturation is the mechanism (not a separate fault) causing the latency

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service protobuf serialization deploy broke pricing-engine quote path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The report's guess: market-data-service v5.2.0 (dep-6111, protobuf serialization switch at 11:56) caused downstream quote slowness. This is contradicted — market-data-service error_rate and latency remained flat, and the pricing-engine fault is CPU-bound inside its own GreeksV2 calculator, not in serialization/deserialization.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: market-data-service telemetry is completely flat (error_rate ~0.2%, p99 ~40ms) and the failing subsystem is pricing-engine's internal GreeksV2 calculator; no serialization/deserialization error appears anywhere.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation from a traffic surge (cf. HIST-113)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: pricing-engine CPU hit 99% due to a genuine traffic/load surge exceeding provisioned capacity, as in HIST-113. Contradicted: request_rate stayed flat at ~640 req/s across the entire window, so load did not grow — the CPU rise is from a per-request cost increase, not volume.

causal_chain.claim: but request_rate did not increase (contradicts surge)

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Request rate is flat (~640 req/s) before and after onset; the CPU jump is explained by per-request GreeksV2 cost, not extra volume.

facts.statement: pricing-engine p99 latency rose from ~60ms to ~1500-2850ms beginning at the 12:00 bucket and stayed elevated through 13:59.
pricing-engine CPU rose from ~40% to ~99% at 12:00 while request_rate remained flat at ~640 req/s.
Config change cfg-3120 set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100 at 12:04:00Z.
pricing-engine logged the cfg-3120 application at 12:04:16.
pricing-engine logged GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo computations of 3-9s and 2000ms-budget deadline-exceeded errors starting 12:05:21.
order-service logged 225 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms' errors starting 12:06:10.
market-data-service error_rate (~0.2%) and p99 (~40ms) were flat across the whole window.
The only deployment was market-data-service v5.2.0 (protobuf) at 11:56, live and not rolled back.
pricing-engine had zero deployments and zero restarts in the window.
order-service p99 rose to ~2900ms while its CPU stayed flat at ~40%.

assumptions: greeks_v2.rollout_pct=100 routes essentially all quote computations to the GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator
CPU saturation in pricing-engine is the mechanism translating the flag ramp into latency; no separate hardware fault is present
the flag value is the operative control knob and was not already overridden elsewhere

timeline.event: market-data-service v5.2.0 (dep-6111, protobuf serialization) deployed — no telemetry impact follows.
pricing-engine logs 'config change cfg-3120 applied: flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct=100'.
First GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo slow warnings (>6s for 20000 paths) and 2000ms budget deadline-exceeded errors.
order-service begins logging 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms'.
Latest data: pricing-engine still ~99% CPU, order-service still timing out; no recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back cfg-3120: set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct back to 5 (or lower) to shed the heavy calculator load.
recommended_actions.rationale: Onset tracks the flag ramp exactly; reverting should restore CPU/latency since the calculator is the CPU consumer.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm recovery by watching pricing-engine CPU (return toward ~40%) and p99 (return toward ~60ms), plus cessation of order-service quote timeouts.
recommended_actions.rationale: Validates the causal chain; if unaffected, H1 is wrong and hypothesis space reopens.

recommended_actions.action: Temporarily raise pricing-engine replica count / CPU limits to absorb GreeksV2 cost while the flag is re-tuned.
recommended_actions.rationale: Buys headroom for the experiment without a full rollback.

recommended_actions.action: Re-tune the GreeksV2 calculator (reduce Monte-Carlo paths, cache results, or lower rollout %) before re-ramping.
recommended_actions.rationale: 20000 paths taking 3-9s per quote exceeds the 2000ms budget by design.

recommended_actions.action: Add a pre-ramp load/CPU guardrail and canary stage for feature-flag rollouts on CPU-heavy code paths.
recommended_actions.rationale: A 5->100 jump masks whether the new path fits the latency budget.

data_gaps: First get_config_changes call was partial (config-audit shard 2/3 did not respond); a retry returned only cfg-3120, so a second concurrent config change could in principle exist but was not seen.
No per-calculator request split metric exists, so the exact fraction of quotes hitting GreeksV2 (pre/post ramp) is inferred from the flag, not directly measured.
No pricing-engine replica count / HPA behavior metric available to fully separate config_change from an autoscaling limitation.

findings.statement: order-service latency_p99 jumped from ~150ms to ~2900ms concurrently with the pricing-engine onset, but order-service CPU stayed flat at ~40%.
Config-change query returned partial:true ('config-audit shard 2/3 did not respond') on first attempt; a retry returned the single cfg-3120 change.

Historical incident HIST-113 (2026-01-28) on pricing-engine had symptoms 'quote timeouts','cpu 99%' attributed to capacity saturation at market open — superficially similar, but its cause (record volume) differs from the flat request rate observed here.
